claim: The Data and Democracy Lab (formerly MGGG, the Metric Geometry and Gerrymandering Group) positions its research explicitly for three audiences relevant to grassroots electoral-targeting applications: communities, policymakers, and courts of law, alongside peer-reviewed academic output.
stance_target: existence of an academic lab whose civic-tech open-source tooling (maup, PyEI) is applicable to electoral-geography crosswalk and ecological-inference problems outside the US
scope_conditions: lab mission statement, current as of fetch date
quoted_support: We develop computational methods to understand how electoral systems function and build tools that make those insights accessible to a wide audience. We aim to make the work useful for audiences like communities, policymakers, and courts of law.
